content.overview: Section 139 requires appointment of an auditor at the first annual general meeting, to hold office until the conclusion of the sixth annual general meeting, with rotation for prescribed classes.
content.glance: Section 139 requires appointment of an auditor at the first annual general meeting, to hold office until the conclusion of the sixth annual general meeting, with rotation for prescribed classes.
content.study: The first auditor is appointed by the board within thirty days of incorporation, failing which by the members. Thereafter the appointment is at the AGM for a term ending at the sixth AGM, subject to ratification as the current text requires; amendment history on annual ratification must be checked. Prescribed classes, including listed companies and stated unlisted thresholds, must rotate the individual after one term of five years and the audit firm after two terms, with a five-year cooling off. The auditor must consent and the company must intimate the Registrar. Casual vacancy is filled by the board, or by a general meeting where the vacancy is caused by resignation. Government companies follow CAG appointment under the section.

examples.title: Resignation vacancy
examples.body: A casual vacancy by resignation is filled by the general meeting, not only the board.

examples.title: Rotation
examples.body: A listed-company audit firm cannot simply continue past two consecutive terms.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who appoints the first auditor?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The board within thirty days of registration. If it does not, the members do.
